import React from 'react';
import { iconSizes } from 'app/theme/foundation';
import {
  ArrowDownIcon,
  ArrowLinkIcon,
  ArrowUpIcon,
  BagIcon,
  BagSelectedIcon,
  BagSolidIcon,
  CalendarIcon,
  CarouselIcon,
  CarouselSelectedIcon,
  ChatIcon,
  CheckIcon,
  ChevronDownIcon,
  ChevronLeftIcon,
  ChevronRightIcon,
  ChevronUpIcon,
  CloseIcon,
  DeleteIcon,
  EditIcon,
  ExternalLinkIcon,
  InfoIcon,
  InfoSelectedIcon,
  InfoSolidIcon,
  LocationIcon,
  MenuIcon,
  MinusIcon,
  MuteIcon,
  PasswordShowIcon,
  PauseIcon,
  PlayIcon,
  PlusIcon,
  ProfileIcon,
  SearchIcon,
  ShareIcon,
  ShareTwoIcon,
  WishlistIcon,
  WishlistSolidIcon,
  PhoneIcon,
  WhatsAppIcon,
  EmailIcon,
} from 'app/components/icons';

// Figma iconography spec: node 1892:59595 — 34 of 34 types implemented.
export type ZimmIconType =
  | 'arrow-down'
  | 'arrow-link'
  | 'arrow-up'
  | 'bag'
  | 'bag-selected'
  | 'bag-solid'
  | 'calendar'
  | 'carousel'
  | 'carousel-selected'
  | 'chat'
  | 'check'
  | 'chevron-down'
  | 'chevron-left'
  | 'chevron-right'
  | 'chevron-up'
  | 'close'
  | 'delete'
  | 'edit'
  | 'external-link'
  | 'info'
  | 'info-selected'
  // Cart-specific custom icon (SFCC-795 rework, plan step 3.2) — found inside the cart
  // inline-message design (Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs), not yet confirmed as part of the
  // generic Figma node 1892:59595 iconography sheet the "34 of 34" count above refers to. Same
  // treatment as the footer-specific trio below.
  | 'info-solid'
  | 'location'
  | 'menu'
  | 'minus'
  | 'mute'
  | 'password'
  | 'pause'
  | 'play'
  | 'plus'
  | 'profile'
  | 'search'
  | 'share'
  | 'share-2'
  | 'wishlist'
  | 'wishlist-solid'
  // Footer-specific custom icons — not yet in Figma node 1892:59595,
  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  | 'phone'
  | 'whatsapp'
  | 'email';

export type ZimmIconSize = keyof typeof iconSizes;

type ZimmIconProps = {
  type: ZimmIconType;
  size?: ZimmIconSize;
  /** Pass Chakra token strings or CSS keywords (e.g. 'text.primary', 'currentColor').
   *  Do not pass hardcoded hex values — use theme tokens. */
  color?: string;
} & ({ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never } | { 'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string });

const ICON_MAP = {
  'arrow-down': ArrowDownIcon,
  'arrow-link': ArrowLinkIcon,
  'arrow-up': ArrowUpIcon,
  bag: BagIcon,
  'bag-selected': BagSelectedIcon,
  'bag-solid': BagSolidIcon,
  calendar: CalendarIcon,
  carousel: CarouselIcon,
  'carousel-selected': CarouselSelectedIcon,
  chat: ChatIcon,
  check: CheckIcon,
  'chevron-down': ChevronDownIcon,
  'chevron-left': ChevronLeftIcon,
  'chevron-right': ChevronRightIcon,
  'chevron-up': ChevronUpIcon,
  close: CloseIcon,
  delete: DeleteIcon,
  edit: EditIcon,
  'external-link': ExternalLinkIcon,
  info: InfoIcon,
  'info-selected': InfoSelectedIcon,
  // Cart-specific — see the ZimmIconType union above for provenance.
  'info-solid': InfoSolidIcon,
  location: LocationIcon,
  menu: MenuIcon,
  minus: MinusIcon,
  mute: MuteIcon,
  password: PasswordShowIcon,
  pause: PauseIcon,
  play: PlayIcon,
  plus: PlusIcon,
  profile: ProfileIcon,
  search: SearchIcon,
  share: ShareIcon,
  'share-2': ShareTwoIcon,
  wishlist: WishlistIcon,
  'wishlist-solid': WishlistSolidIcon,
  // Footer-specific custom icons — not yet in Figma node 1892:59595,
  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  phone: PhoneIcon,
  whatsapp: WhatsAppIcon,
  email: EmailIcon,
} as const;

/** Atom — single icon from the Zimmermann icon set. Mirrors zimm-icon contract. */
export const ZimmIcon = ({ type, size = 'md', color = 'currentColor', ...aria }: ZimmIconProps) => {
  const Icon = ICON_MAP[type];
  // Both keys exist in every member of the union (one required, one optional-`never`), so the
  // rest object is indexable directly. The XOR is enforced by ZimmIconProps, not by a cast —
  // casting here only widened 'aria-hidden' from `true | undefined` to `boolean | undefined`.
  const ariaHidden = aria['aria-hidden'];
  const ariaLabel = aria['aria-label'];
  return (
    <Icon
      boxSize={iconSizes[size]}
      color={color}
      aria-hidden={ariaHidden}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      role={ariaLabel ? 'img' : undefined}
    />
  );
};

1	/**
2	 * Guard: a multipart recipe's declared `parts` must cover every part the component actually
3	 * reads off `useMultiStyleConfig`.
4	 *
5	 * The failure this catches is silent, though not by the mechanism it looks like: `parts` does
6	 * not gate `baseStyle`. Probed directly against `ChakraProvider`, a recipe declaring
7	 * `parts: ['declared']` while carrying both parts in `baseStyle` and in a variant resolves to
8	 * `{declared: {...base, ...variant}, undeclared: {...base}}` — the undeclared part keeps its
9	 * full base styling and loses only the variant's. `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`. The base
10	 * SFCC `theme/components/project/header.js` is that same shape shipping in production: 9
11	 * declared `parts` against 13 `baseStyle` keys, and the four it omits (`accountIcon`,
12	 * `arrowDown`, `signoutIcon`, `signoutText`) are each read, spread and styled by
13	 * `components/header/index.jsx` (lines 232, 255, 321, 323) today.
14	 *
15	 * So an undeclared part goes wrong in one of two ways, both quiet. If `baseStyle` covers it, it
16	 * renders correctly and then stops responding to variants and sizes — latent on a recipe with no
17	 * variants today, surfacing only the day someone adds one. If `baseStyle` does not, the read is
18	 * `undefined`, `__css={undefined}` is a legal prop, and the element inherits. Neither is reported
19	 * by `tsc`, eslint, an axe run, or a `play` that only asserts text. The first case is precisely
20	 * the "would survive a refactor invisibly if broken" case .claude/rules/testing.md says to cover,
21	 * so the corrected mechanism strengthens this guard's justification rather than weakening it.
22	 *
23	 * Comparing `parts` against the recipe's own `baseStyle` keys would not catch it: renaming a
24	 * part in both places at once keeps them consistent with each other and still breaks the
25	 * component. The component's reads are the only source of truth for what it needs, so this
26	 * walks the component source.
27	 *
28	 * Scope: `overrides/app/components/**` — every co-located `<name>.css.ts`, which since the
29	 * footer decomposition is where a component's recipe normally lives.
30	 *

/**
 * Guard: a multipart recipe's declared `parts` must cover every part the component actually
 * reads off `useMultiStyleConfig`.
 *
 * The failure this catches is silent, though not by the mechanism it looks like: `parts` does
 * not gate `baseStyle`. Probed directly against `ChakraProvider`, a recipe declaring
 * `parts: ['declared']` while carrying both parts in `baseStyle` and in a variant resolves to
 * `{declared: {...base, ...variant}, undeclared: {...base}}` — the undeclared part keeps its
 * full base styling and loses only the variant's. `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`. The base
 * SFCC `theme/components/project/header.js` is that same shape shipping in production: 9
 * declared `parts` against 13 `baseStyle` keys, and the four it omits (`accountIcon`,
 * `arrowDown`, `signoutIcon`, `signoutText`) are each read, spread and styled by
 * `components/header/index.jsx` (lines 232, 255, 321, 323) today.
 *
 * So an undeclared part goes wrong in one of two ways, both quiet. If `baseStyle` covers it, it
 * renders correctly and then stops responding to variants and sizes — latent on a recipe with no
 * variants today, surfacing only the day someone adds one. If `baseStyle` does not, the read is
 * `undefined`, `__css={undefined}` is a legal prop, and the element inherits. Neither is reported
 * by `tsc`, eslint, an axe run, or a `play` that only asserts text. The first case is precisely
 * the "would survive a refactor invisibly if broken" case .claude/rules/testing.md says to cover,
 * so the corrected mechanism strengthens this guard's justification rather than weakening it.
 *
 * Comparing `parts` against the recipe's own `baseStyle` keys would not catch it: renaming a
 * part in both places at once keeps them consistent with each other and still breaks the
 * component. The component's reads are the only source of truth for what it needs, so this
 * walks the component source.
 *
 * Scope: `overrides/app/components/**` — every co-located `<name>.css.ts`, which since the
 * footer decomposition is where a component's recipe normally lives.
 *
 * It is not a whole-repo guard, and nothing else covers the remainder: the model is strictly
 * sibling-based (a recipe's `parts` are reconciled against the `index.tsx` beside it), so a
 * recipe that does not sit next to its component is out of reach. `theme/components/header.ts`
 * is the only multipart recipe in that position today and is therefore unguarded.
 * `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` does not pick it up either — that suite has no
 * parts-vs-reads check of any kind; it guards bare token keys and recipe namespacing.
 *
 * `READ_RE` recognises only the identifier `styles`, so a second binding in the same component
 * is invisible here: `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx` reads `chrome.actions`. That one is
 * deliberately out of scope rather than a gap to close — `chrome` holds *ZimmModal's* recipe,

## Overall: PASS

Nothing here needs to go back to the Implementer. The one open item — Design fidelity — isn't something a rework instruction can close; only Marcel's own look can, exactly as it did last time.

## What I tried to falsify

- Re-ran `tsc`/`test`/`lint`/`audit:tokens` myself rather than trusting the restated counts. Lint: baseline stated as 966/896/70 → fresh run is 963/896/67 (net *better*, not just "same"). I didn't stop at the totals — I traced every finding inside a touched file back to source: `product-item/index.tsx:171,191` and `index.stories.tsx:158` all predate this rework (pre-existing `onItemQuantityChange`/template-literal/`require-await` warnings from earlier commits, confirmed by reading those exact lines). No new warning is hiding inside a net-improved total.
- Read `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s actual `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`/`PROP_COMBINATIONS` source (lines 226-252) to check the code comment's claim that `hasError` is one of 5 exhaustively-walked boolean keys (32 combinations) — confirmed verbatim, not an invented-sounding justification.
- Read `foundation/typography.ts:143-149` to check whether `caption` textStyle really defaults to medium weight — confirmed, so the recipe's `fontWeight` override is fixing a real divergence, not a phantom one.
- Grepped `CODEOWNERS` directly for `icons` and `item-variant` instead of accepting the Orchestrator's "no entry" claim at face value — zero matches for either. The gap is real.
- Read `.claude/session-notes.md:395` directly — it says "warning state (grey info icon + message...)" verbatim, exactly as the citation claims. Real, pre-existing corroboration, not a manufactured one.
- Checked the icon-only-on-warning condition can't leak to error: read the actual JSX (`variant === 'warning' &&`) and cross-checked against the dedicated "error never renders the icon" test.
- Checked whether splitting the recipe into `root`/`text` silently changed the error (no-icon) case's visual output versus the old single-node shape: `color` is set only on `root`; `text` declares no competing `color`, so the paragraph inherits it via ordinary CSS inheritance — behaviour-preserving, not just additive.
- Checked `iconSizes.md = 16px` and `spacing.xs/s/m/xl = 8/12/16/24px` directly against the foundation files rather than trusting the arithmetic in comments.
- Checked whether this diff crosses more than one protection tier without cover: it touches `product-item/` (Tier 2, Squad B) + `theme/components/index.ts` (Tier 2, UI designer) + `ui-kits/` (Tier 3) — exactly the combination `plan.md` §3 already pre-clears for B3 ("One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away"), not a new crossing introduced by this rework.

## What I could not verify

- Design fidelity itself — no rendering tool available to me in this session, and this is explicitly Marcel's gate, not a Scorer's.
- The Figma MCP tooling referenced in my environment's system instructions was not actually a callable tool in this invocation, so I could not re-pull node `9323:106685`'s metadata myself. I corroborated the citation through internal consistency across all 3 files that reference it and the independent line-395 corroboration instead, not a fresh Figma read of my own.
- I did not re-run the Tester's Playwright suite, mutation testing, or a real Chromium accessibility-tree probe — deliberately, since the brief scoped my own re-verification to the cheap four, and redoing an already-completed battery on an unchanged claim would itself be the over-run this project is trying to stop. I'm relying on the Tester's report for that layer.
- I did not redo the Tester's repo-wide "no other latent crash from this import chain" grep myself; the full green 1302/1302 Vitest run is a strong independent proxy but isn't the identical check.

## Defects

None found requiring rework.

Consequence first: if the icon is wrong in some way no automated check catches — wrong stroke weight, a colour that passes its token-name check but is the wrong token, anti-aliasing that reads differently from Figma — it ships, because every gate that ran here (mine and the Tester's) proves the code matches the *numbers* cited from Figma, not that a human glancing at both side by side would wave it through. That's the same gap category this whole rework exists to close.
